name: MathlibAnnex.Plucker.exists_extension_with_derivativeAverage_mem
title: One boundary extension with all five analytic properties

content.display_title: One boundary extension with all five analytic properties
content.one_sentence_role: Keeps boundary agreement, contraction, derivative control, integrability and average membership on one witness.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n,N\in\mathbb N_0$ and give $E=\mathbb R^n$ and $F=\mathbb R^N$ their coordinate sup norms. Let $\lambda_n$ be the fixed coordinate Lebesgue measure on $E$. Let $p:E\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous real seminorm with specified constants $a_p,b_p>0$ such that
$$a_p\|x\|_\infty\le p(x)\le b_p\|x\|_\infty\qquad(x\in E).$$

The lower bound makes $p$ a norm. Its closed unit ball and real reference volume are
$$K_p=\{x:p(x)\le1\},\qquad v_p=\lambda_n(K_p)\in(0,\infty).$$
Here and below a finite Lebesgue measure is read as a real number when used as a scalar. The boundary is the unit sphere $\Sigma_p=\{x:p(x)=1\}$.

Let $\mathcal I_{n,N}$ be the finite set of increasing $n$-tuples of distinct rows from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. The minor-coordinate space $\mathbb R^{\mathcal I_{n,N}}$ carries its sup norm. For a linear map $B:E\to F$, put $B_{ij}=(Be_j)_i$ in the standard coordinate basis. Write $\Pi_n(B)$ for its maximal-minor vector and $\mathcal V_p(B)$ for that vector scaled by $v_p$. Their coordinates and scaling are
$$\Pi_n(B)_I=\det(B_{i_a,j})_{a,j=1}^n,\qquad\mathcal V_p(B)=v_p\Pi_n(B)\quad(I=(i_1<\cdots<i_n)).$$

A $p$-contraction is a linear map $B:E\to F$ satisfying $\|Bz\|_\infty\le p(z)$ for every $z\in E$. Write $\mathcal C_p^N$ for these maps. Write $\mathcal G_p^N$ for the signed generator set and $\mathcal P_p^N$ for its real convex hull, so
$$\mathcal G_p^N=\{\mathcal V_p(B),-\mathcal V_p(B):B\in\mathcal C_p^N\},\qquad\mathcal P_p^N=\operatorname{conv}_{\mathbb R}(\mathcal G_p^N).$$

For any function $k:E\to F$, write $Dk(x)$ for its Fréchet derivative where it exists and for the zero linear map otherwise. Write $G_{p,k}$ for its derivative-generator function and $\mathcal A_p(k)$ for the average of that function over $K_p$. The integrand and normalization are
$$G_{p,k}(x)=v_p\Pi_n(Dk(x)),\qquad\mathcal A_p(k)=v_p^{-1}\int_{K_p}G_{p,k}(x)\,d\lambda_n(x).$$
The integrals use the fixed reference measure, even when distances are measured with $p$.

Let $h:\Sigma_p\to F$ satisfy $\|h(u)-h(v)\|_\infty\le p(u-v)$ for all $u,v\in\Sigma_p$. There is one function $f:E\to F$ with all five properties:
$$\begin{aligned}
&\|f(x)-f(y)\|_\infty\le p(x-y)&& (x,y\in E),\\
&f(u)=h(u)&& (u\in\Sigma_p),\\
&\|Df(x)z\|_\infty\le p(z)&& (z\in E),\quad\lambda_n|_{K_p}\text{-a.e. }x,\\
&G_{p,f}\in L^1(K_p,\lambda_n),\\
&\mathcal A_p(f)\in\mathcal P_p^N.
\end{aligned}$$
content.assumptions: The source and target are finite real coordinate spaces with sup norms. The seminorm $p$ is continuous and has the stated positive lower and upper comparison constants. The measure is the original coordinate Lebesgue measure. The boundary map is $1$-Lipschitz for the $p$-distance and the coordinate sup norm on $F$. No differentiability of $h$, nonempty sphere, or positive dimension is required. The dimensions $n,N$ may be zero. When $n=0$, the unique empty minor has determinant $1$; when $N<n$, the minor-index set is empty and its function space has one element. Neither case is excluded.
content.conclusion: The single extension $f$ satisfies the displayed five properties simultaneously. Its average is taken over $K_p$ with reference Lebesgue measure. This asserts existence of a common witness, not uniqueness.
content.proof_summary: Extend coordinatewise in the induced norm, return to reference coordinates, then derive the remaining properties for that same function.

proof_steps.text:
**Construct an extension in the correct metric.** On the same vectors of $E$, use the distance $d_p(x,y)=p(x-y)$. If $\Sigma_p$ is empty, take $f=0$. Otherwise write $h_i$ for coordinate $i$ of $h$ and, for $1\le i\le N$, use
$$f_i(x)=\inf_{u\in\Sigma_p}\bigl(h_i(u)+p(x-u)\bigr).$$
Fix $u_0\in\Sigma_p$. The boundary Lipschitz inequality and the triangle inequality give, for every $u\in\Sigma_p$,
$$h_i(u_0)-p(x-u_0)\le h_i(u)+p(x-u).$$
The infimum is finite: this is a lower bound, and $u=u_0$ gives a finite upper bound. For $v\in\Sigma_p$ and $u\in\Sigma_p$,
$$h_i(v)\le h_i(u)+p(v-u),\qquad f_i(v)\le h_i(v)+p(v-v)=h_i(v).$$
Taking the infimum in the first inequality yields $f_i(v)=h_i(v)$. For any $x,y\in E$, the triangle inequality in the defining formula gives
$$f_i(x)\le f_i(y)+p(x-y),\qquad |f_i(x)-f_i(y)|\le p(x-y).$$
The second bound follows by also interchanging $x$ and $y$. Hence the coordinate map $f=(f_i)_{i=1}^N$ satisfies
$$\|f(x)-f(y)\|_\infty\le p(x-y),\qquad f|_{\Sigma_p}=h.$$
For $N=0$ the target is the zero space and these assertions still hold, without taking a maximum of an empty family. [The scalar McShane construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/360da6fa66c1273b76b6b2d8c5666fd5ac2e3b56/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Lipschitz.lean#L306-L337) and [its finite-coordinate version](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/360da6fa66c1273b76b6b2d8c5666fd5ac2e3b56/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Lipschitz.lean#L342-L353) prove precisely these extension properties. The source theorem chooses a witness of that result; all following steps use that one $f$, read in the original reference coordinates.

**Pass this same extension to its derivative.** The first output gives
$$\|f(x)-f(y)\|_\infty\le p(x-y)\le b_p\|x-y\|_\infty.$$
[The reference-norm Lipschitz conversion](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Module/EquivalentSeminorm/Topology.lean#L48-L59) supplies a global $b_p$-Lipschitz bound. Apply [the almost-everywhere directional bound](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/SeminormBound.lean#L60-L71) with the same $f$, seminorm $p$, upper constant $b_p$, and restricting set $K_p$. Its output is the third property, $\|Df(x)z\|_\infty\le p(z)$ for all $z$, almost everywhere on $K_p$.

**Prove integrability for this witness.** Let $C\ge0$ bound the compact generator set $\mathcal G_p^N$. The derivative bound just obtained gives
$$G_{p,f}(x)\in\mathcal G_p^N,\quad\|G_{p,f}(x)\|\le C\quad\text{a.e. on }K_p,$$
$$\int_{K_p}\|G_{p,f}(x)\|\,d\lambda_n(x)\le C v_p<\infty.$$
The total derivative is measurable; continuous volume-scaled minors make this finite-coordinate vector strongly measurable. [Compactness of the signed generators](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Convex/PluckerBody.lean#L66-L90) supplies $C$, and the ball has finite measure. These are the actual inputs of [integrability under the seminorm increment bound](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/Average.lean#L58-L81), which yields the fourth property for the same $f$.

**Average without changing the witness.** We now have
$$G_{p,f}\in L^1(K_p),\qquad Df(x)\in\mathcal C_p^N\quad\text{a.e. on }K_p.$$
Apply [derivative-average membership](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/Average.lean#L39-L56) to exactly these two outputs. It gives $\mathcal A_p(f)\in\mathcal P_p^N$. Together with the two extension properties in Step 1, this is one existential witness with all five conclusions.

content.lean_realization_notes: The radial extension of a sphere isometry is a separate construction. This theorem does not identify its witness with a radial map.
